overview.description: Cross-cutting conventions for component prop APIs, so prop names and shapes are predictable across the whole library instead of decided fresh per component.

rules.name: Use native `disabled`, not `isDisabled`
rules.description: Disabled state must be exposed as the native `disabled` prop/attribute, not a custom `isDisabled` boolean.
rationale: `disabled` is a real HTML attribute: it works with forms, the `:disabled` CSS pseudo-class, and testing-library's toBeDisabled() out of the box.
Re-typing a custom `isDisabled` prop after Omit-ing the native `disabled` attribute is extra code for no behavioral gain.
Checkbox, Switch, and Radio already use `disabled` directly; it is the majority pattern, not the exception.

knownViolations.resolution: migrate to `disabled` next time Button is touched
migrate to `disabled` next time IconButton is touched

rules.name: Reserve `is*` prefix for component-owned state
rules.description: The `is*` boolean prop prefix (e.g. isLoading, isFullWidth, isExpanded) should only be used for state that is custom to the component's own visual/behavioral logic — not for anything that maps directly to a native HTML attribute.
rationale: Native attributes (disabled, checked, required, readOnly) already have an established name; renaming them with an `is*` prefix adds a translation layer with no benefit.
Custom component state (loading, full width, expanded) has no native equivalent, so an `is*` prop is the clearest way to name it.

examples: disabled (Checkbox, Switch, Radio) — native attribute, not isDisabled

questions: Does this prop correspond to a native HTML attribute?
If yes: use the native name as-is.
If no: is this state genuinely specific to this component's own behavior?
If yes: an `is*`-prefixed boolean is appropriate.
decisionFramework.defaultDecision: Prefer the native attribute name whenever one exists.
decisionFramework.principle: Don't invent a prop name where HTML already has one.
